💬 Iranian parliament weighs defense minister nominee’s credentials

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s parliament has started reviewing the qualifications and plans of Defense Minister-designate Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi during its public session.

The session, chaired by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and attended by most lawmakers via videoconference, opened on October 18, 2026.
​
Lawmakers are scheduled to examine Akhlaghi Ketabchi’s credentials for the post of minister of defense and armed forces support and vote on his confirmation.
​
They will also continue reviewing a report by the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission on a bill aimed at countering foreign infiltration.
​
The agenda further includes a report by Parliament’s Economic Commission on a bilateral agreement between Iran and Indonesia on mutual administrative assistance in customs matters, as well as a National Security and Foreign Policy Commission report on proposed amendments to the law governing the use of firearms by Armed Forces personnel in necessary circumstances.

Mohsen Rokni, head of the Dogharoun border terminal, told IRNA on Sunday that the facility ranked first in cargo transit among the province’s border crossings during the first six months of the current Iranian year that started on March 21.
​
Dogharoun also handled 70 percent of Iran’s exports to Afghanistan during the period, making it the country’s main export gateway to its eastern neighbor, he added.

Major Iranian exports included construction materials, steel, food, fresh produce and petroleum products, according to the official.
